answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that later counterparties validate and by staking a bond that is slashed when audits find fabricated work. A new identity therefore starts with no reputation, and splitting effort across many accounts does not multiply trust: each account must repeat the costly work and risk its own stake. A basalt ledger can record bonds and outcomes, while a whisper of collusion is not enough to punish anyone without evidence; even an orchard of fake agents must pay the real cost of earning and risking credibility.
